memory_candidates.content: To deterministically reproduce a git-commit-time staging drop for testing, plant a `pre-commit` hook that mutates the TEMPORARY partial index git builds for a `git commit -- <pathspec>` invocation (the hook runs with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing at that temp index, exported by git). `git update-index --cacheinfo <mode> <sha> <path>` inside the hook reverts a path to a stale blob; `git update-index --force-remove <path>` drops a never-before-tracked path entirely. This is 100% deterministic, unlike a probabilistic concurrent-writer race, and directly exercises the documented-but-easy-to-miss fact that `git commit -- <pathspec>` re-reads the working tree fresh at commit time rather than committing whatever `git add` last staged.

When building a pre-commit intent snapshot of 'what files a pathspec array is about to affect', enumerate via the UNION of `git ls-files`, `git diff --name-only HEAD`, and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, each restricted to the pathspec array, and run this BEFORE `git add` touches the index -- not after. Timing is load-bearing: run post-add, the enumeration for a rename pathspec pair (old+new path together) silently loses the vacated source half (it's no longer in the pre-add index by the time you look); run pre-add, `git ls-files` still shows the old tracked path (about to become a deletion) while `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` already shows the new untracked path, correctly capturing both halves of the rename in one pass.

A test assertion that greps a script's output for a bare diagnostic-label substring (e.g. "V8") to mean 'this specific gate fired' is fragile: any OTHER message in the same script that happens to mention that label by name (e.g. a corrected comment pointing a reader at the new gate) will make the assertion pass/fail for the wrong reason. Always match the diagnostic's own marked prefix pattern (e.g. "ERROR:.*V8") instead of the bare label.
